_disclaimer: FICTIONAL developer, invented for this R&D project. Any resemblance to a real company is unintended. The visual language is generic modernist (cream paper, black geometric mark, lowercase grotesk); the mark itself is original to this project.
name: form and order

tagline.es: casas que ya sabían cómo vivirse
tagline.en: houses that already knew how to be lived in
tagline.pt: casas que já sabiam como ser vividas

positioning: A developer that restores Buenos Aires heritage typologies and sells them as they are: long, narrow, full of light and patios. Modern graphics, old architecture.

typography.license: Fontshare free license (desktop + web, commercial use allowed)
typography.note: Neutral grotesk, close to the reference's Söhne-like feel. Wordmark and headlines lowercase; data uppercase with wide tracking.

mark.concept: Option A: a square with two opposite corners cut by quarter discs - order is the square, form is the curve. Drawn from code in pipeline/brand_mark.py, no external asset, no resemblance to any existing logo.
mark.clearspace: half the mark's width on every side

do: talk about light, patios, proportions and the street
spanish rioplatense for AR, neutral for PT/EN
dont: luxury clichés (exclusive, unique opportunity, dream home)
promises about the neighbourhood's future value

ai_disclosure.es: Imagen generada con IA a partir del modelo 3D del proyecto.
ai_disclosure.en: AI-generated image based on the project's 3D model.
ai_disclosure.pt: Imagem gerada com IA a partir do modelo 3D do projeto.

legal.rule: Every published asset carries the AI disclosure. Geometry must match the 3D model (that is what the quality gate enforces): no invented rooms, balconies, windows or amenities.
